newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks dragged down by blue chip selling.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks dragged down by blue chip selling.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks edged down in early Wednesday trade due to selling of a highly capitalised blue chip, brokers said.

The all share index was 1.08 points down at 604.12 at the mid-morning break. Hayleys Ltd, a high cap blue chip, fell five rupees to 175, dragging down the index, which is weighted towards market capitalisation, they said.
"The Hayleys' sale was by a retail investor, probably getting liquid for the December holidays," said Ajit Dias Wanigasekera, a trader at Commercial Stock Brokers.
Turnover was 7.4 million rupees on 262,658 shares, supported by 75,000 shares of Sampath Bank, which traded one rupee up at 46.
A parcel of one million shares of Kelani Tyre was on bid at six rupees.
"There are buyers who are using the seasonal lethargy to get into the market," said a trader at John Keells.
